    Triangulated embeddings force surjective projections (Theorem 3.1, (1) ⇒ (2)) #

    Let (F, η) : C(D) → T be a triangulated embedding. The interval conflations A i → P i → Y go to distinguished triangles with connecting morphisms δ_i = η(ε_i), and (a_{ji})_* ε_j = ε_i gives δ_j ≫ (F a_{ji})⟦1⟧ = δ_i. For u ∈ D_i, the composite X → A i → P i vanishes, so (F u)⟦1⟧ = v ≫ δ_i for some v : FX⟦1⟧ → FY. The morphisms v ≫ δ_j come from a compatible family (u_j) with u_i = u.

    Statement.ProjectionsSurjective D

    Theorem 3.1, (1) ⇒ (2). If C(D) has a triangulated embedding into a pretriangulated category, then every projection lim D → D_i is surjective.
